name: PEI / ULTEM
bestUses: Industrial heat-resistant technical parts; printer and end-use qualification required. This entry remains excluded from H2C printing.
limitations: Excluded from H2C. Industrial printing profile only.

summary.text: PEI / ULTEM is polyetherimide. Makers sell it for medical tools that withstand autoclave and gamma sterilisation, for electrostatic-discharge protection, and for aerospace and automotive parts. Its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 208 °C. On the H2C it is out of reach: most products ask for 370⁠–⁠380 °C at the nozzle, and more bed heat than the printer gives.

items.text: Ideal for use in critical applications which require electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection, a high level of cleanliness, and the outstanding thermal and chemical properties you’ve come to expect with PEI based compounds.
Long-term hydrolytic stability
High thermal properties, with a Tg of 217C
Inherently flame-resistant
Excellent dimensional stability, low heat creep sensitivity, and a very low, uniform coefficient of thermal expansion create highly reproducible part-to-part dimensions
Exceptional strength and modulus, even at elevated temperatures
Good resistance to a broad range of chemicals, include automotive fluids, fully halogenated hydrocarbons, alcohols, and aqueous solutions
Stable dielectric constant and dissipation factor over a wide range of temperatures and frequencies
PEI is an amorphous, high-performance polymer that combines excellent mechanical, thermal, and chemical resistance properties.
Our PEI based filaments offer the ability to create parts with excellent properties at elevated temperatures due to a very high glass transition temperature (Tg).
Drying Specs 150C for 4 hours
Nozzle Specs No special concerns
Heated Chamber Recommended
PEI 9085 has a translucent colour of amber and it is widely used in application such as medical, electrical/electronic, automotive, and aerospace industries.
PEI 9085 is a high-performance material that have excellent thermal properties, exceptional dimensional stability, good chemical resistance, and inherent flame retardancy.

items.text: These properties make the 3D 4 MAKERS PEI Filament particularly suitable for usage in FDM and FFF 3D printers.
Polyether Imide (PEI) Ultem 1010 is an amorphous, amber to transparent thermoplastics with a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 217 °C and performs in continuous use up to 170 °C.
This inherently flame retardant plastic has UL94 V0 and 5VA ratings.
The material has an excellent adhesion between layers
The material has an excellent adhesion between layers which results in great improvement of the impact resistance, strength, durability and the printing process.
The 3D 4 MAKERS PEI Filament has unique properties because it does not come into contact with water during the production process and is directly packaged in a vacuum packaging.
Drying recommendations 120°C, minimal 4 hours
When the 3D printer is not being used it is important to keep the 3D4MAKERS PEI Filament in a bag and stored in a cool, dry and dark place until it is used again.
This cannot be a room where people sleep.
To get the best results while printing we advise you to keep the 3D printer in a room where there is hardly any draft and/or temperature fluctuations.
Keep the 3D printer out of the sun.
High dimensionally stable precision parts.
During processing the moisture level should not exceed 0.03%, otherwise porosity and surface defects (e.g. smearing) may occur.
Predrying is recommended even when sealed original containers are being used.
